K1 Area Map Fixes - what this patcher writes, byte for byte
===========================================================

Published so that a collision with another executable patcher is diagnosable
by someone who is not us, and so that a determined user can undo or reproduce
the work by hand. k1hrm publishes its offsets for the same reason; this is that
precedent, followed.

THE BUILD THIS DESCRIBES
------------------------
The "KOTOR Editable Executable" (4,042,752 bytes) after UniWS and after KotOR
High Resolution Menus (k1hrm) 1.5 have both been run on it. The patcher refuses
any other size. GOG's own retail v1.03 swkotor.exe is this same file byte for
byte - confirmed by direct comparison, the only difference is 16 bytes of
unused PE header padding - so it's accepted directly with no unlocking step.
The 4-CD retail build hasn't been measured and the patcher still refuses to
guess at it.

After this patcher runs, the file is 4,050,944 bytes - 8 KB larger. That growth
is step 5 below and is the only change to the file's size.

TWO ADDRESS CONVENTIONS, AND WHY YOU MUST NOT MIX THEM
------------------------------------------------------
Numbers below are labelled VA (virtual address, what a disassembler shows) or
FILE (byte offset into swkotor.exe, what a hex editor shows).

For everything in the original sections,   FILE = VA - 0x400000.
For the reserved region in step 5 it is    FILE = VA - 0x492000,
because that region lives in a section this patcher extends. The exe is only
0x3DD000 bytes long, so subtracting 0x400000 from 0x86D000 lands past the end
of the file and finds nothing. Both numbers are given for it below.

WHAT IS WRITTEN
---------------

0. k1hrm's Area Map centring constants - ONLY IF k1hrm LEFT THEM VANILLA

   FILE 0x2928B3, 0x292959   int16, X   vanilla 640 -> your width
   FILE 0x2928C3, 0x29296B   int16, Y   vanilla 480 -> your height

   These four are k1hrm's, not ours. Its hires_patcher.pl writes them; its
   compiled hires_patcher.exe - the one its own .bat and readme point Windows
   users at - does not. Left vanilla, the engine draws the Area Map
   ((W-640)/2, (H-480)/2) pixels off its box.

   This patcher writes them only when they hold exactly 640/480 AND the canvas
   constants already prove k1hrm ran at your resolution. Any other value is
   refused rather than guessed at. Recorded in installed.json as its own step;
   Uninstall.bat puts 640/480 back, which restores k1hrm's broken state, not a
   fixed one.

1. Map scale (the Area Map filling its box) + the private float copies

   16 scale constants inside the Area Map draw path are rewritten for your
   resolution. The two shared floats the map divides by -

   VA 0x747748  (440.0)   FILE 0x347748
   VA 0x7455D4  (256.0)   FILE 0x3455D4

   - are NOT rewritten. They are shared with the HUD minimap, and editing them
   in place turns the minimap black. Instead, scaled copies are written to
   private slots and only the Area Map's own operands are redirected at them:

   VA 0x78CC00  FILE 0x38CC00   private X float
   VA 0x78CC04  FILE 0x38CC04   private Y float
   (VA 0x78CC00-0x78CC0F / FILE 0x38CC00-0x38CC0F is reserved for these.)

1b. Marker icon size - ONLY AT RESOLUTIONS THAT NEED IT

   15 immediates covering all three marker kinds - map notes, the player arrow
   and party members - are multiplied by

       s = clamp(ceil(min(kx, ky) / (1600/480) - 0.25), 1, 8)

   where kx = width/640 and ky = height/480. s is 1 at 2560x1600 and below,
   and at s = 1 not one byte is written. Across k1hrm's 49 resolution sets:
   36 unchanged, 9 at x2, 3 at x3, 1 at x6.

   The three marker materials are mm_barrow (player arrow), lbl_mapcircle
   (unselected note, and party - they share it) and whitetarget (selected
   note). They are ordinary textures and resample cleanly.

2-3. Three marker calibration caves, in spare .text

   hook (5 bytes, jmp)          cave
   VA 0x6946D3  FILE 0x2946D3   VA 0x73C1D0  FILE 0x33C1D0   map-note markers
   VA 0x694A42  FILE 0x294A42   VA 0x73C20C  FILE 0x33C20C   party markers
   VA 0x694AB1  FILE 0x294AB1   VA 0x73C232  FILE 0x33C232   player arrow

   Total cave region occupied: VA 0x73C1D0-0x73C2A9, FILE 0x33C1D0-0x33C2A9.
   Every byte of it read 0x00 before this patcher ran, and the patcher refuses
   if it does not.

4. 8 KB reserved at the end of .rsrc

   VA 0x86D000   FILE 0x3DB000   0x2000 bytes
   First 16 bytes: the ASCII magic K1MAPNTS then 8 reserved bytes.

   The section's virtual and raw sizes and SizeOfImage are grown to match. No
   other section header changes, and the PE CheckSum field is deliberately left
   alone (see COMPATIBILITY.txt).

5. The map-note correction table and its match routine

   250 corrections, 16 bytes each = 4,000 bytes, written into the region above
   at FILE 0x3DB010 onward.
   Table sha256 880a325d982d74df496b02782faefdd3ae3802efbba030b9fbccc967cc0ccaa5

   Each entry is four little-endian floats: the note's stored world X and Y as
   BioWare shipped them (the lookup key), and the corrected X and Y.

   The match routine is assembled into the cave region and hooked in at

   VA 0x6946EF  FILE 0x2946EF   5-byte jmp, resuming at VA 0x6946F4

   It compares the note's stored position against the table and substitutes the
   corrected pair on a hit. A note not in the table is left exactly as it was,
   so the patch is inert for every note it does not correct.

   The keys are world positions, not module or index numbers, which is why the
   table survives mods that edit module files. Verified against Kotor 1
   Community Patch 1.10.0: of the 4,064 waypoints K1CP touches or leaves,
   it moves 35, none of which is a map note, and all 250 corrections still
   match afterwards.

AFTER WRITING
-------------
The patcher re-reads the file from disk and runs 21 checks against it,
including a check that no byte outside the ranges listed above changed. If any
check fails it says so and points you at the backup; it does not report success
on an unverified write.

VERIFYING BY HAND
-----------------
The install record installed.json - in %LOCALAPPDATA%\K1AreaMapFixes, beside
the backup it names - lists every step, its offsets, the sha256 of the exe
before and after, and the relative path to the backup. Uninstall.bat restores
that backup; it does not attempt to undo the changes byte by byte.

Both live outside this folder deliberately: the mod folder is a download, and
people delete downloads. Set K1AMF_HOME to put the pair somewhere else.

REPRODUCING THIS FROM SOURCE
----------------------------
The patcher carries no byte-level constants of its own. Every offset above
lives in the same modules the project's own development and verification tools
use (tools\hires_patch.py, tools\pe_space.py, tools\note_table_patch.py), so a
shipped patcher and a verified binary cannot drift apart. The source is in
this release under "More info\source\".
